payload.instructions: Preserve all candidate IDs and distinctions. Broader parent themes organize evidence; they do not imply measurement equivalence.

themes.disagreements: contradictions, weak signals, and proxy distinctions
evidence_ids: at most 12 representative supplied modeling evidence IDs
themes.interpretation: common or complementary evidence
themes.name: theme

themes.disagreements: Effect modification signals are present but moderate (support fractions ~0.4), suggesting their role as confounders may be equally prominent.
themes.interpretation: Measurements regarding the presence and size of adrenal nodules show consistent evidence of influence on treatment assignment, outcome prognosis, and effect modification.
themes.name: Adrenal-related Indicators

themes.disagreements: Age is a powerful confounder, while history of AKI, appetite status, and anthropometrics show weaker or non-replicated signals.
themes.interpretation: Core demographics, functional status, and psychosocial indicators acting primarily as confounders or prognostic factors, with evidence for treatment-effect heterogeneity specifically for anxiety.
themes.name: Patient Demographics and Baseline Status

themes.disagreements: Strong signals for ALC and mutation status contrast with the negligible independent signal for rearrangement status and procedural metadata.
themes.interpretation: A group of markers showing a split between strong prognostic value (ANC), treatment-effect heterogeneity (ALC, mutation status), and weak proxies with insufficient evidence for a causal role.
themes.name: Hematological and Genomic Biomarkers

themes.disagreements: Acetaminophen and alcohol use are primarily confounders, while antidiabetic use is an instrument-like predictor without outcome impact.
themes.interpretation: Prior medications and comorbidities showing varied roles as confounders, prognostic factors, or markers of heterogeneous treatment effects.
themes.name: Prior Therapeutic and Medical History

themes.disagreements: High-magnitude signals for intracranial lesions and bone pain contrast with the very weak signals for actionable molecular markers.
themes.interpretation: Indicators of disease location and lesion severity demonstrating strong prognostic importance and significant evidence of effect modification.
themes.name: Anatomic and Symptomatic Disease Burden

themes.disagreements: Strong confounding by GFR and BP contrasts with a more distinct effect modification signal for BUN in R-learners.
themes.interpretation: Physiological and metabolic indicators that strongly predict both treatment assignment and outcome, functioning primarily as confounders.
themes.name: Physiological and Metabolic Indicators

themes.disagreements: Robust signals for axial structure abnormalities contrast with very weak or non-evaluable signals for atrial fibrillation.
themes.interpretation: Structural abnormalities and historical medical markers showing mixed evidence as potential effect modifiers or prognostic factors.
themes.name: Structural and Historical Findings

themes.disagreements: Brain metastases presence (052) and cerebral imaging (071) provide prognostic signals, while location (051), calvarium lesions (057), and brainstem signal (054) show evidence for effect modification. Conversely, features 063, 067-070 predominantly predict treatment assignment.
themes.interpretation: Structural and radiographic markers of CNS involvement, manifesting as a mix of prognostic factors, treatment confounders, and effect modifiers.
themes.name: CNS and Neuro-Imaging Characteristics

themes.disagreements: Total comorbidity count (082) and clinical phenotype (079) are strong confounders. Fatigue (060) and deconditioning (099) are primarily prognostic, though 099 and hemodynamics (100) also demonstrate effect modification.
themes.interpretation: General health, frailty, and systemic status markers that serve as either prognostic factors or confounders, with some evidence of treatment-heterogeneity.
themes.name: Systemic Health and Comorbidity Burden

themes.disagreements: CMP results (084) act primarily as a confounder. CK5/6 expression (076) is a strong effect modifier. Renal markers (095, 096) and molecular markers (064, 065) show a dual role as both confounders and effect modifiers.
themes.interpretation: Laboratory and pathological markers including organ function and molecular expression, predominantly serving as confounders or effect modifiers.
themes.name: Pathological and Laboratory Markers

themes.disagreements: COPD markers (087, 088) are consistent confounders and prognostic factors. Confusion (085) is identified as an effect modifier, while cough productivity (091) and other neurological markers (094, 098) show weak or inconsistent signals.
themes.interpretation: Respiratory health and acute neurological presentation, where COPD acts as a confounder and acute confusion suggests treatment effect modification.
themes.name: Respiratory and Acute Symptomology

themes.disagreements: Carboplatin (061) is a strong prognostic factor. Cancer diagnosis (058), calorie intake (056), and cycle count (073) primarily serve as markers for treatment assignment (confounders).
themes.interpretation: Clinical oncology characteristics and treatment history, exhibiting a split between prognostic value and treatment prediction.
themes.name: Oncology and Treatment-Related Factors

themes.disagreements: Varying strength of treatment prediction, with disease_status (102) showing a weaker signal than ecog_performance_status (109).
themes.interpretation: General disease status and quality-of-life domains that strongly correlate with both treatment assignment and outcome prognosis, suggesting confounding roles.
themes.name: Systemic Status and Quality of Life

themes.disagreements: Employment status (114) is a dominant confounder, whereas emphysema (113) specifically shows strong evidence for effect modification.
themes.interpretation: Metabolic vitals and baseline comorbidities serving as strong prognostic markers and common causes of treatment assignment.
themes.name: Metabolic and Comorbidity Markers

themes.disagreements: Dyspnea severity (108) exhibits strong evidence for both confounding and effect modification, whereas general dyspnea (106, 107) primarily shows confounding.
themes.interpretation: Respiratory and hematologic indices showing consistent prognostic importance, with graded severity providing signals for treatment heterogeneity.
themes.name: Respiratory and Hematologic Indices

themes.disagreements: EGFR mutation (111) shows a credible signal for effect modification and prognosis, while enzyme elevation (115) is largely uninformative.
themes.interpretation: Genomic and molecular markers reflecting distinct causal roles, from treatment selection (confounding) to response heterogeneity (effect modification).
themes.name: Tumor and Genomic Profiling

themes.disagreements: Recurrence (101) is supported by R-learners and causal forests, while dizziness (103) is supported by univariable effects; feature 139 is largely inconsistent.
themes.interpretation: Clinical markers and family history that primarily signal treatment-heterogeneity without strong main-effect confounding.
themes.name: Clinical Effect Modifiers

themes.disagreements: GERD (144) is purely prognostic, whereas globe appearance (145) shows signals across all roles and head shape (148) is primarily a treatment predictor.
themes.interpretation: Physical examination and anatomical findings with mixed support, ranging from simple prognosis to complex effect modification.
themes.name: Physical and Anatomical Attributes

themes.disagreements: Feature 126 is a very strong treatment predictor but lacks an outcome signal, suggesting it may be an instrument rather than a confounder.
themes.interpretation: Candidates exhibiting high support for treatment assignment, with varying degrees of outcome prognosis and treatment heterogeneity.
themes.name: Strong Treatment Drivers

themes.disagreements: Feature 123 shows a penalized main treatment signal, but lacks complementary outcome or effect signals.
themes.interpretation: Candidates with low overall support or signals primarily limited to outcome prognosis without strong treatment prediction.
themes.name: Weak or Prognostic-Only Signals

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
